nn/{ocgtl,encoder,signet,gladc}.py are byte-for-byte copies from
GAOOD/nn. nn/cvtgad.py has only a device-placement patch: attention temperature
k is a registered buffer, and device comes from the caller rather than global
CUDA availability. It also has normalized line endings. See provenance.json
for upstream/local hashes and commits of the four active author repositories.
The unused GOOD-D core and its adapter branch have been removed.

Licenses: UB-GOLD's MIT LICENSE is retained. OCGTL-derived code (ocgtl.py and
myGIN/GraphNorm portions of encoder.py) originates in Bosch's AGPL-3.0 code;
its license and third-party notice are retained in licenses/. Original SIGNET,
GLADC and GOOD-D MIT notices from the source distribution are also retained.
CVTGAD's author checkout has
no license file; the imported version is from the MIT-licensed UB-GOLD release.
The UB-GOLD MIT notice does not replace upstream notices.

Adapter protocol (src/models/benchmarks/ubgold.py):
- Existing local TU features/splits; no graph labels supplied to models.
- Fixed final epoch, no test-selected checkpoint or hyperparameter search.
- Adam, model-specific fixed YAML budgets; not a paper reproduction.
- Training shuffles all normal graphs and merges a singleton final minibatch
  into its predecessor; no normal graph is discarded or duplicated.
- SIGNET uses endpoint-averaged node features as edge features (the official
  input_dim_edge=0 branch), consistently with other local node-feature models.
  Edgeless graphs receive self loops so their dual hypergraph is nonempty.
- CVTGAD structural encodings follow UB-GOLD's sparse random-walk
  diagonal and degree one-hot code, with zero inverse degree for isolates.
- SIGNET/CVTGAD evaluation scores each query with eight fixed normal
  training references; queries do not interact with other test graphs. This
  differs from the released test-batch contrastive scoring. Context, training
  loss normalization statistics are checkpointed.
- GLADC preserves padded reconstruction and perturbed-encoder contrastive
  training. Perturbed parameters are copied without storage aliasing and do
  not accumulate unused gradients. Inference reduces node errors per graph
  (equivalent to official batch-size-one scoring), supporting arbitrary batch
  sizes. Padding is fixed by the dataset config; oversize graphs fail clearly.

Paper figures come from UB-GOLD Table 3 (arXiv:2406.15523v2). Its Section 3.3
explicitly tunes hyperparameters on the test set to report upper bounds.
Those figures are motivation for inclusion, not expected unbiased local scores
or evidence that every selected method is a current 2026 state-of-the-art leader.
